jobs.occupation: Student Assistant for the International Recruitment team
jobs.description:
The AU International Student Recruitment team is looking for a new student assistant to help with the AU Student Ambassador Network and other tasks.

The student assistant will be part of the International Recruitment team in the Recruitment and Guidance department. The team consists of 5 full-time staff members and around six student assistants.

Primary tasks

You will play an important role in the day-to-day coordination of the AU Student Ambassador Network. The Student Ambassador Network brings together international students at Aarhus University who help prospective students learn more about studying at Aarhus University and student life in Denmark.

Your tasks will include:

• Staying in regular contact with our Student Ambassadors and following up on their activities on Unibuddy

• Helping recruit and onboard new Student Ambassadors

• Helping plan and carry out events for the Student Ambassador Network

• Helping arrange Instagram takeovers

• Supporting international student events and activities across AU, such as Intro/ Welcome Days, webinars and campus tours

• Assisting with practical and administrative tasks related to international student activities and communication

The tasks vary throughout the year, so you should enjoy a role that combines communication, hands-on event support, coordination and administration!

Expected qualifications

We expect that you:

• Have experience using Excel, Forms, PowerPoint, Teams, and other digital tools

• Have excellent written and spoken English

• Are organized and detail-oriented, and comfortable keeping track of several ongoing tasks

• Can communicate confidently by email and through online platforms

• Are responsible, reliable and able to take initiative

• Are approachable and comfortable communicating with students from different countries and cultural backgrounds

• Are flexible, as some activities and events may take place outside normal office hours

It is an advantage if you:

• Have previously participated in the AU Student Ambassador Network

• Have experience organizing events or student-led initiatives

• Have been involved in student organizations or volunteer networks

As our Student Assistant, you will get the opportunity to:

• Work independently while being part of a collaborative team

• Work closely with international students from across AU and build a broad network

• Gain hands-on experience with event planning and coordination

• Work with Unibuddy and other digital platforms used in international student recruitment

• Develop your communication, administrative, organizational and intercultural skills

Location

Your place of work will be the Recruitment and Guidance Office at Frederik Nielsens Vej 5, 8000 Aarhus C

Pay

The position is paid according to the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and HK (read the collective agreement here).

Who can apply

The AU International Office encourages students who have at least one year left of their studies in Denmark to apply for the position. Please note that you need to be a full-time student at a higher learning institution in order to apply.

If you have any questions - please contact:

Gitte Bindzus Foldager, International Communications and Student Recruitment Manager

jobs.occupation: Senior Composite Process Technology Manager, FPRT
jobs.description:
Do you know why a composite part fails before it fails? Own the composite process technology in a new, safety-critical production in Vojens and build it from the ground up.

Southern Jutland

Permanent employment

Full time

26-11-2026

Share

Moment Professionals is recruiting on behalf of FPRT a Senior Composite Process Technology Manager for the new composite production in Vojens, Denmark. We are looking for a composite specialist with real depth in the technology who can convert transferred know-how into controlled, scalable and repeatable industrial processes. The role suits you if you want to build a production from the ground up and would rather build processes where little is written down yet than step into a production where everything is already in place.

Your everyday at FPRT

You report to the Chief Production Officer, Composite Manufacturing, and you build and lead the composite technology team of composite process engineers and materials and polymer engineers. You work closely with Production, Quality and NDT, HSE, Maintenance and Engineering, Planning and Supply Chain, and you support the competency and qualification standards for supervisors, technicians and operators together with Production and HR. You are the technical authority for composite manufacturing processes, with the mandate to define process parameters, technical standards and work instructions, and to require technical containment, a process review or a production stop when process integrity, product quality or safety is at risk.

Production starts from an existing process that is being transferred to Vojens, and experienced specialists from the group come to the site to hand it over. You lead the technical transfer and convert it into FPRT-controlled specifications, work instructions, training content and qualification requirements, and you define the technical requirements for equipment, tooling, fixtures, utilities and production conditions through trials, pilot builds and ramp-up. You make sure FPRT has clear local ownership of the critical processes and keeps the technical knowledge for the long term. From day one, you are expected to spot where a step can be done smarter and to have the composite understanding to back that view.

Your time is split between the desk and the floor. You own process flows, critical parameters, material requirements and process-control standards, and you define process qualification, inspection points, acceptance criteria and quality gates together with Quality and NDT. When a process starts to drift, you are the primary escalation point: you go to the floor, lead root-cause analysis, non-conformity investigations and corrective actions, and turn the lessons into updated standards and training. The weight of the role lies in the moulding stage and the material side of the process: resin systems, reinforcements such as carbon fibre, adhesives, curing and the conditions that decide whether porosity and voids are designed out or created. You need a sound grasp of finishing, but your depth is in why a part comes out of the mould as it does.

This is a greenfield site. New buildings are under construction on the site, systems are being selected, and support functions such as maintenance, IT and HR are being built in parallel. In the first period you will help shape how things are done well beyond your own field, and the composite team grows as production scales towards stable serial production.

The role is based in Vojens, and being on site is essential during the build-up. English is the working language in instructions and with colleagues across the group. Danish is a strong advantage in daily life on the floor, and if you are not fluent yet, your willingness to learn it counts.

And then there are the benefits:

Real authority over the processes you own, greenfield impact with no legacy to work around, a professional, international environment with a clear mission and purpose, a modern office with gym, sauna and social spaces, and top-of-market compensation for the right experience.

To succeed in the role…

…you do not need to have carried a manager title or to come from defence. What matters is that you know composite technology in depth: why a resin system behaves as it does, what creates strength and what creates defects, and how the environment affects the part. You may come from composite manufacturing in wind energy, marine, aerospace, defence or another high-performance industry, and work today in process or manufacturing engineering, production, materials or as a technical composite specialist. You also take pride in:

• 
challenging an established method, including one handed over by experienced colleagues, and agreeing on a better answer together.

• 
taking ownership and making decisions where little is written down yet.

• 
going to the floor when a process drifts and staying until the root cause is found.

• 
turning know-how into standards, instructions and training that engineers and operators can work from.

• 
developing engineers through technical reviews, coaching and structured problem solving.

What you need to bring:

• 
Either a relevant technical degree or equivalent strong industrial experience, and at least five years in composite manufacturing, process engineering, manufacturing engineering or materials engineering.

• 
Practical experience with industrial manufacturing of fibre-reinforced composite components and thermoset resin systems such as epoxy, phenolic or other thermosets, and hands-on experience with one or more of resin infusion or transfer processes, filament winding, lay-up, moulding, curing, bonding or composite machining and finishing.

• 
A proven track record of developing, transferring, industrialising, qualifying or stabilising manufacturing processes into repeatable production, with a solid grip on process control, documentation, process risk assessment, root-cause analysis, non-conformity handling and technical change management.

• 
Experience leading, mentoring or coaching engineers and production specialists, or acting as their technical authority.

• 
Fluent English, written and spoken. Danish is a strong advantage, or the willingness to learn it.

It is an advantage if you:

• 
come from advanced composite manufacturing in wind energy, marine, aerospace, defence, pressure vessels, automotive or another high-performance application.

• 
have worked with large or structurally critical components, such as aerospace and defence structures, casings, filament-wound products, UAV components or wind turbine blades.

• 
have taken part in a greenfield factory, a new production line, a technology transfer or a major ramp-up.

• 
live within commuting distance of 6500 Vojens, Denmark.

The process may include interviews with Moment Professionals and FPRT, relevant tests and reference checks.

Due to the sensitive defense-tech nature of FPRT's projects and operations, all potential employees are subject to a police and intelligence background check as part of FPRT's standard recruitment process. Continued employment is conditional upon obtaining and maintaining the necessary security clearance.

AFTERMARKET MANAGER

If you thrive with great responsibility for service operations, customer relationships and continuous improvement of our aftermarket offering – and you're not afraid to open a terminal and write a bit of code yourself – we have the role for you right here.

You will work with the organization to build a strong, proactive service setup, develop our aftermarket revenue (spare parts, service agreements and upgrades) and ensure our customers get fast, competent support. You will be a key point of contact for our customers, handling incoming calls and e-mails and making sure their issues are solved quickly and professionally. Because our vision systems combine hardware with advanced software, you will also get close to the technical core of our solutions – diagnosing issues, building small tools and scripts, and working with our developers to solve problems at the source.

Your areas of responsibility

You will lead and develop the Service department and be the driving force behind our aftermarket strategy. Specifically, you will:

-       Manage and priorities the daily service tasks and the service technicians handling installation support, troubleshooting and maintenance at customer sites.

-       Have personnel management responsibility for the Service department – including staffing, development, one-on-ones and the day-to-day motivation and wellbeing of your team.

-       Be a direct point of contact for customers by phone and e-mail, handling enquiries and support cases and solving their problems quickly and professionally.

-       Own the aftermarket business – service agreements, spare parts sales and upgrade opportunities – and identify ways to grow this area.

-       Act as an escalation point for complex technical and software-related support cases, including remote diagnostics on our vision systems.

-       Write and maintain scripts and small tools (e.g. in Python or similar languages) that support diagnostics, service reporting and internal workflows.

-       Explore and apply AI tools to make service and support more efficient, e.g. for faster troubleshooting, case handling and internal knowledge sharing.

-       Collaborate closely with the software and hardware development teams to feed field experience back into product improvements.

-       Implement and continuously optimize processes to secure documentation, approvals and full delivery of service commitments.

-       Build and maintain long-term relationships with customers and sub-suppliers involved in service and support.

Professional competencies required

You hold a relevant technical education – for example within electronics, mechanical, production or software engineering – or you have equivalent experience from a similar role in the automation, machine vision or industrial technology industry.

You are comfortable with coding and can read, write and debug scripts (Python or similar) to solve practical problems – you don't need to be a professional software developer, but you're not intimidated by code and enjoy using it as a tool. You also have a genuine interest in AI and how it can be used practically to streamline service, support and diagnostics.

You have experience with technical service, support or maintenance, ideally including personnel management responsibility for a team or a service function. You are used to handling direct customer contact by phone and e-mail and enjoy solving customers' problems. Experience with spare parts sales, service agreements or other aftermarket business is an advantage, as is knowledge of the food and packaging industry.

Personal profile

You are service-minded and thrive when you can make customers succeed with our technology. You take ownership naturally and genuinely enjoy people management – motivating, developing and creating a good everyday life for your team – whether you already have managerial experience or have the clear potential and drive to take on the responsibility.

You are structured and good at prioritizing in a busy day with many parallel cases, and you keep a cool head when issues get technical or time critical. You communicate clearly and diplomatically with both customers and colleagues – on the phone, by e-mail and in person – and you're just as comfortable in a technical discussion with a developer as in a friendly, problem-solving conversation with a customer.

Practical information and application

The position is reporting to the Operations Director of TriVision A/S. You will be based in Odense, and we expect you to start in the new position as soon as possible.

For further questions regarding the role, you are welcome to contact Operations Director Torben Poulsen at 2779 5898.

jobs.description:
Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

**The Opportunity

**Veo's security surface is unusual. We train models on-premise on dedicated GPU infrastructure, run the product across AWS and GCP, and operate a fleet of tens of thousands of cameras deployed at clubs and venues worldwide. That is a scope most SaaS security engineers never touch: physical devices in the field, heavy on-prem compute, and multi-cloud production, all in one role.

We are forming a Security Enablement Team that makes it easier for every engineering and IT team at Veo to build, ship, and operate secure systems. You will own the infrastructure and cloud security slice, where office networks, data center networks, and employee access to product systems meet, partnering with the teams that own these systems so security is built in from the start. As an enablement function, the team does not run these systems day to day. We build the paved roads, tooling, and patterns that let the owning teams operate securely by default.

You will join during a pivotal moment. We are standing the team up, defining what good looks like across infrastructure, network, and workforce identity security, and rolling out the first paved roads for a unified internal network across our datacenters (GCP, AWS) and offices (Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen), workforce identity and access, and drift checks for cloud configuration and network rules. You'll have direct impact on how 100+ engineers, and every Veo employee, work securely across our offices and clouds.

**What You Will Do

**You'll join the Security Enablement Team and focus on the infrastructure and cloud security slice, where office networks, data center networks, and employee access to product systems meet. Everything below follows the same pattern. We design the paved road, prove it works, and hand it to the team that will own it. We share ownership of the team's work, pair on complex problems, and rotate responsibilities. The systems themselves stay with the owning teams, and our job is to make those teams successful.

• Lead the design, reviews, and tooling for our office and data center networks and the VPN that connects them, as part of the network security direction the team sets together. Day-to-day operation and firewall changes stay with the team that owns the network

• Build patterns and tooling for secure cross-site connectivity and endpoint security posture that IT can adopt and run, in a way that supports how Veo engineers actually work

• Build the patterns and automation for workforce identity and access, including SSO hygiene, MFA enforcement for employees, and clean joiner, mover, and leaver flows for access to product systems, with IT owning the day-to-day operation

• Build automated checks that surface drift in cloud configuration and network rules, so the owning teams get a signal and can act on it

• Act on infrastructure and network findings from external penetration tests, routed through the team's shared intake, with the owning teams driving remediation

• Build the first version of cross-cutting capabilities, such as the cross-site VPN or the drift checks, then hand each one to a long-term owner with a written transition that covers the runbook, ownership, and escalation path

• Partner with GRC to build evidence pipelines for IT and access-related controls that produce auditable output without manual follow-up

• Run office hours where IT, platform, and product teams can get a network or access review

As the team matures, you'll help shape how Veo's network and identity stack evolves across our offices and clouds as the company grows.

**What You Could Bring

**This role deliberately sits where IT, cloud, and security meet. You do not need to be world class at all three. You are strong in one or two and comfortable operating across the rest.

You likely have several years of experience at that intersection. That tends to show up in several of the following:

• Solid IT fundamentals: networking, identity, endpoint posture, MFA, and SSO at production scale

• Cloud infrastructure experience: hands-on work on at least one of GCP or AWS, including IAM, networking, and basic Terraform-style IaC

• Workforce identity and access: hands-on experience with SSO and identity providers (Okta, Google Workspace) and clean joiner, mover, and leaver flows

• A security mindset layered on that IT and cloud depth: you instinctively look for misconfigurations, drift, and bad access patterns, without needing to be a dedicated security specialist

• Cross-context comfort: you can work on an office network problem and a product cloud problem in the same week without context-switching pain

• Platform-as-product mindset: you've built internal tooling that real teams adopt, with guard rails built into the tools people already use and manual review as a last resort, and you gathered feedback and measured impact

• Comfort handing work back to a long-term owner once the build phase is done

• Collaboration: you work through discussion and feedback, share context effectively, and write things down.

Nice to have: VPN solutions at scale (Tailscale, Cloudflare Access, WireGuard), endpoint management tooling, and audit log pipelines.

**How We Work

**You'll join a Copenhagen-based Security Enablement Team of three engineers plus a manager. We operate as an enablement function: we build shared tooling and golden paths, and we step in for focused, high-leverage missions where no other team is positioned to deliver. We do not run a SOC and we do not carry a security pager.

You'll collaborate regularly with the Platform, Product, IT, Firmware, and GRC teams. We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

If you read that list and matched on most of it but not all of it, apply anyway. People who span IT, cloud, and security are rare, and we do not expect every box ticked. We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

Do you want to be a valued part of the critical infrastructure that serves communities across Europe and beyond? Are you looking for a position in which you can set direction and help shape our company? If so, then you could be the newest addition to our team as

**Senior Frontend Engineer – Tracking.

****Be part of the movement - and play your part.

****About The Role

**As a Senior Frontend Engineer – Tracking at DFDS, you will join a collaborative team working at the intersection of frontend engineering, customer data, analytics, and marketing technology. This is a role for someone who enjoys both hands-on implementation and seeing the bigger picture: how platforms, tracking, data flows, consent, and customer experiences connect to create better and more personalised journeys.

You will play an important part in strengthening our Martech foundation and helping us build more scalable and data-driven customer experiences across our digital platforms. The team is working on initiatives such as improving our customer data platform foundation, enabling more personalised experiences, and building reliable tracking and consent setups that allow us to work smarter across channels.

**On a Day-to-day Basis, You Will

**

• Help establish and evolve a strong CDP foundation, with Twilio Segment experience considered a strong advantage.

This role is well suited to a senior profile who enjoys working across disciplines and who can combine implementation skills with architectural thinking.

“We’re looking for someone who enjoys solving problems together, can see the bigger picture across customer data and platforms, and still loves getting hands-on with implementation.”

**About You

**We think the strongest teams are built on diversity and inclusivity. Contrasting opinions, varied skills and strong characters bring out the best in us all. And we cannot wait for you to join.

To succeed in this role, your experience, technical depth, and ability to connect frontend development with Martech plays key role.

**We Are Looking For Someone Who Has

Working at DFDS At DFDS, you will be part of an environment where technology, collaboration, and business impact go hand in hand. This role offers the opportunity to work on meaningful digital initiatives that influence how we engage with customers across channels and platforms.

• Meaningful scope: Help shape the Martech and customer data foundation behind important digital journeys.

• Modern collaboration: Work closely with colleagues across engineering, analytics and marketing.

• Growth opportunities: Develop your skills in frontend engineering, customer platforms, data flows, and personalisation.

• A collaborative culture: Join a team that values learning, shared decisions, and knowledge exchange.

• Attractive office environment: Work from our headquarters in Copenhagen, with modern facilities and a strong in-person team culture.

While you’re with us, we want you to develop. At DFDS, we believe that development happens first and foremost through activities in the workplace. We will also offer training courses that can support you in your role, if needed.

Are we a match? Then what are you waiting for? Apply Now.  If you think your personality, skills, experience, and desire match this role, we’d love to hear from you. Please send us your CV as soon as possible, as we’re keen to meet potential candidates on an ongoing basis.

For questions regarding the technical scope or team culture, feel free to reach out to Frontend Chapter Lead, Noman Ahmed Khan at nkhan@dfds.com. Please note that we only consider applications submitted directly through our official recruitment system.

jobs.description:
The Human Centered Computing Section at the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI.

  The start date is expected to be 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.
  

  The position

  This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions.

   

  Project description

  The PhD student’s research is expected to conduct in-depth qualitative studies of how EU digital regulation (e.g., AIA, DSA) is technically and organisationally implemented in SMEs developing AI-related technologies. The goal is to map developers’ translation of regulatory guidance into product and service design and compares implementation strategies across sectors. This project offers a focused route into human-centred computing, sociotechnical research and the study of regulation in practice. You will join an international cohort, receive supervision across institutions and take part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment.

  The PhD student to be recruited in this call is expected to define their PhD project within the scope of the overall project and collaborate with the larger project team.

   

  Description of the scientific environment

  The position will be within the Human Centered Computing section (HCC). The Human Centered Computing section is a highly interdisciplinary group that conducts research within the areas of Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Supported Cooperative Work, Ubiquitous and Pervasive Computing, Digital Fabrication and related fields. Our section aspires to be a top research environment that bridges technology, theory, and empirical studies. The Human Centered Computing research environment at the University of Copenhagen is internationally leading, as evidenced by it’s ranking as second in Europe according to CSRankings. Further information about research at the Department is available here: https://di.ku.dk/english/research/ .

  This position will be co-supervised by Irina Shklovski (email: ias@di.ku.dk) and Naja Holten Møller (email: naja@di.ku.dk) at the University of Copenhagen in the Department of Computer Science, Human-Centered Computing section. The PhD will be conducted in collaboration with Joris Van Hoboken, Professor of Information Law, with special emphasis on Law and Digital Infrastructure at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Faculty of Law, University of Amsterdam

   

  Who are we looking for?

   	
• Applicants should hold a MSc degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Data Science, HCI, Critical Data Studies, STS, Law and Policy or a related field. 	
• Good written and oral English skills are a requirement. 	
• Previous scientific publications (if any) and relevant work experience is encouraged 	
• Applicants must be willing to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities   The ideal candidate would have an educational background or prior work experience in technology development, prior experience in qualitative research and fieldwork in organisations, and some understanding of European regulatory and policy concerns around AI systems.
  

  The PhD programme

  You can undertake the PhD programme as:

  A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish Master’s degree.

  Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme equivalent to a Danish Master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the position, i.e. HCI or CS. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Additional qualifications for the MSCA PhD 

  REGULAIRE is funded by the European Commission’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie programme and to be eligible for this funding you must meet the following criteria:

   	
• You must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to your recruitment; 	
• You must work on the project full-time.   Please ensure that this information is clear on your CV. Researchers can be of any nationality.

   

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as a PhD fellow is full time, on site in Copenhagen, and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific position formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

   	
• Carry out a research project with increasing autonomy from your supervisors 	
• Collaborate with researchers both within the research group, and with external project partners 	
• Author scientific papers aimed at high-impact venues 	
• Participate in the research and training activities with the REGULAIRE network 	
• Disseminate research nationally and internationally 	
• Attend PhD courses on general skills development such as academic writing, as well as relevant specialised courses such as REGULAIRE summer and winter schools 	
• Conduct a change of scientific environment in the form of a secondment with a relevant standards organisation and an extended visit with one of the REGULAIRE academic partners 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project    

  We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD position 	
• Relevant educational background 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• Good written and oral English language skills    

  Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Cover Letter detailing your motivation and background for applying for this PhD position; 	
• Research Statement detailing your desired research focus and goals for the PhD studies within the scope of the specified position. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research direction within technology governance you wish to explore, including: specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature, and the potential impact and applications; 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position; 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted; 	
• Publication list (if available); 	
• Names and contact details of three references.    

  Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is November 22, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by unbiased expert assessors. You will be notified about whether your application will be selected for assessment.

  The assessors will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessments. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in December

   

  Questions

  For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact ias@di.ku.dk  

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

**Job Description

**Do you want to define the evaluation methodology and technical requirements that underpin effective AI evaluation and monitoring within the business at one of the leading financial institutions in the Nordics?

Join Danske Bank's newly established AI Model Assessment team in Business Controls & Product Management. As AI Evaluation Methodology & Platform Requirements Lead, you will hold a 1st Line of Defence role with clear ownership of the technical methodologies used to evaluate AI models and AI-enabled solutions, and of the technical requirements for the platforms that support their evaluation and ongoing monitoring. You will translate business-owned risk and control needs into clear methods, metrics, data, evidence, traceability and platform capabilities that can be implemented consistently across the Bank's technology landscape.

This is a unique opportunity to shape a consistent, scalable and evidence-based capability through which the business identifies, evaluates, monitors and manages AI model risk.

This role can be based in Copenhagen, Denmark, Vilnius, Lithuania, Warsaw, Poland, Stockholm, Sweden or Helsinki, Finland.

**What You Will Be Doing

**The AI Model Assessment team is a business-owned control capability that performs evidence-based assessments of AI models and AI-enabled solutions across the Bank. We work with business owners, developers, engineers and platform teams to understand how solutions operate, define the evidence required for assessment, and establish the evaluation and monitoring capabilities needed to identify, assess and manage model risk where it arises.

Our mission is to enable responsible innovation by providing the business with a consistent and scalable framework for evaluating AI systems, monitoring their performance and risk, and demonstrating that appropriate controls are operating effectively.

As AI Evaluation Methodology & Platform Requirements Lead, you will own the evaluation methodology and define the technical requirements for the platforms, tooling and data capabilities used by the 1st Line of Defence to evaluate and monitor AI models and AI-enabled solutions. Your mandate is to ensure that the business has robust, implementable and auditable means to assess its AI risks and controls. Your focus will be on specifying what the evaluation and monitoring capability must deliver rather than owning software development or platform operations.

You will work closely with the independent 2nd Line AI model risk function, which sets the overarching risk framework and provides oversight and constructive challenge. You will translate that framework into practical evaluation methodologies, technical requirements and business-owned controls, provide transparent evidence of how requirements are implemented, and support the resolution of identified gaps.

**Your responsibilities will include:

**

• Owning, developing and maintaining the methodology for evaluating AI models and AI-enabled solutions, including evaluation objectives, test approaches, acceptance criteria and evidence standards.

• Defining the functional and technical requirements for evaluation and monitoring platforms that enable risk management, including data ingestion, test execution, metric calculation, observability, evidence capture, reporting, access controls and auditability.

• Translating model risk, business and assessment requirements into reusable evaluation methods, representative datasets, metrics, thresholds, monitoring indicators and structured evidence requirements.

• Determining how AI system architectures, components, dependencies and data flows affect evaluation scope, test design, monitoring coverage and the technical capabilities required from supporting platforms.

• Defining platform-agnostic requirements that support evaluation and monitoring across environments such as AWS Bedrock and AgentCore, Databricks, Azure OpenAI and embedded third-party AI platforms.

• Setting requirements for reproducibility and end-to-end traceability across models, prompts, datasets, configurations, system components, evaluation results, monitoring signals and changes over time.

• Prioritising opportunities to standardise and automate evaluation and monitoring activities, and working with evaluators, platform owners and engineers to convert approved control requirements into practical platform capabilities.

• Engaging with the Second Line model risk function to interpret applicable requirements, demonstrate how they are operationalised, respond to constructive challenge, and ensure that evaluation and monitoring evidence supports effective independent oversight.

**About You

**An experienced AI evaluation, model risk, data, architecture or platform professional who can establish rigorous evaluation methodologies and turn business risk and control needs into clear, implementable technical requirements for enterprise platforms and tooling.

You have:

• Proven experience designing or governing AI/ML evaluation methodologies, including test objectives, datasets, metrics, thresholds, acceptance criteria and evidence standards.

• Experience translating evaluation, monitoring, risk and control needs into functional and technical requirements for platforms, tooling, data pipelines and reporting capabilities.

• Experience with AI/ML evaluation, business-owned model risk management and controls, technical assurance, MLOps, LLMOps, AI platforms or AI observability.

• Familiarity with cloud AI services or enterprise AI platforms; experience with AWS Bedrock or AgentCore, Databricks or Mosaic AI, Azure OpenAI, or comparable platforms is an advantage.

• Strong understanding of evaluation and monitoring principles, including representative datasets, experiment configuration, metric design, regression testing, monitoring indicators, traceability and evidence capture.

• Ability to distinguish methodology and requirements ownership from platform implementation, while collaborating effectively with engineers and platform owners. Python or similar tools for analysis, prototyping or investigation are an advantage, but software development is not the primary focus of the role.

• Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to articulate evaluation, monitoring, risk and control requirements across business, assessment, platform, engineering, architecture, data and risk functions.

Experience with AI evaluation or observability technologies, for example Phoenix or comparable tools, is an advantage but is not a prerequisite.

**What We Offer You

**You will join the newly established AI Model Assessment team in Business Controls & Product Management, helping build the Bank's consistent and scalable business-owned capability for AI evaluation, monitoring and model risk management.

The team combines technical AI evaluation expertise with model risk management and works across the Bank's AI initiatives. In this role, you will connect evaluators with platform, engineering, architecture and data teams by defining the methods and technical requirements their solutions must support, ensuring that risk ownership and control evidence remain anchored in the business.

If hired in Lithuania, your monthly salary would range from 4320 EUR to 6480 EUR gross (based on your competencies relevant for the job).

Additionally, each Danske Bank employee receives employee benefits package which includes:

• Growth opportunities: professional & supportive team, e-learnings, numerous development programs; (incl. professional certificates); 100+ professions for internal mobility opportunities.

• Health & Well-being: a diverse, inclusive, work & life balance work environment; additional health insurance; mental well-being practices; partial psychologist counselling compensation; silence and sleep zones at the office; game rooms.

• Hybrid working conditions: Work from home up to two days a week; home office budget (after the probation period); modern Danske Campus workplace developed with anthropologist for the best employee experience.

• Additional days of leave: for rest, health, volunteering, exams in higher education institutions, and other important activities. Moreover, for seniority with Danske Bank.

• Monetary compensation package: accidents & critical diseases insurance; financial support in case of unfortunate events, travel insurance; IIIrd Pillar Pension Fund contribution.

See all the benefits HERE**.

**Your job function (position) in the job contract will be AI Science

**Are you ready for the next step?

**If you are passionate about defining robust AI evaluation methodologies and the technical requirements for scalable evaluation and monitoring platforms that support effective business ownership of AI risk, we would love to hear from you.

For questions about the role, please contact Khaled Alizai, Head of AI Model Assessment at khali@danskebank.dk. We are screening the applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply.

Join us and help build the business-owned foundation for effective AI model evaluation, monitoring and risk management at Danske Bank.
